title: First-Day Jitters? These Fifth Graders Have a Plan!
summary:
Imagine walking into a big, new school on your very first day. Scary, right? At Micheltorena Street Elementary in Los Angeles, they have a super cool way to help little kids feel brave. Fifth graders become "toolbox coaches" for the new kindergarteners. They hold their hands, walk them to class, and even share their favorite toys.

Principal Nichole Sakellarion started this tradition 11 years ago. She saw that the youngest students were nervous about starting school. So she decided to welcome them a day early. That way, they could meet their buddies and find their cubbies before the big day.

Ten-year-old Noemi Ulloa is a toolbox coach. She remembers feeling shy when she started at this school. Now she wants to help others. "As a toolbox coach, I think I can help kindergartners harness their emotions," she said. That means helping them understand and manage their feelings.

Gerald Gomez-Reina is another coach. He teaches the little kids tricks like taking deep breaths. He even has a special trick called "garbage can." "That's when you throw away feelings, if you get sad or mad," he explained. He also brought his stuffed raccoon, Rocket, to help calm any nerves.

On the real first day, parents were crying at the gate, but guess what? Almost no tears from the kindergarteners! They walked in holding hands with their fifth-grade buddies. Now that's a great way to start the school year!

Across the country, about 54 million students are heading back to school. Some ride bikes in a "bike bus" in Oklahoma. But at Micheltorena, they have something even better: a buddy to help you through the day.
why_it_matters: Everyone knows what it feels like to be the new kid, and this story shows that even a friendly smile, a buddy, or a deep breath can help someone else feel safe.

background_read: Many schools in the United States have buddy programs where older students help younger ones feel at home.
Starting at a new school is a big change, and having a familiar older friend can make the first day much less scary.
Some communities even use fun ideas like a 'bike bus,' where children ride bicycles to school together in a group.
Article_Structure: WHO: Fifth graders at Micheltorena Street Elementary, including Noemi Ulloa and Gerald Gomez-Reina, are the toolbox coaches.
WHAT: They welcome kindergarteners a day early, walk them to class, share toys, and teach calming tricks like deep breaths.
WHERE: Micheltorena Street Elementary, a school in Los Angeles.
WHY: To help young students feel less nervous and learn to handle their emotions on the first day of school.

perspectives.description: They get a friendly fifth-grade buddy on their very first day, so school feels less scary and more exciting.
The older students get to be leaders and helpers, and they learn that helping others also helps them understand their own feelings.
Parents may cry at the gate, but teachers see fewer tears when kids have older buddies to walk in with.
